text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Shipping group A.P. Moeller shipyard, Lindoe Vaerftet, is the only Danish shipyard to have received more state subsidies than the European Union allows, the EU commission told trade minister Jan Troejborg on Monday. EU investigations on Danish state subsidies to shipyards started last year, when the European commission criticised Denmark for giving unauthorised subsidies to its shipyards
--- The parliament plans giving access for media and citizens to meetings in its many committees, which have been closed to the public until now.

--- More than 40 companies near Denmark's second largest city, Aarhus, plan to start advertising campaigns to gain political support for a new airport in the area fearing that the Aarhus region will waste away if local politicians drop all plans for an international Aarhus airport.
--- Banking analysts expect the crown to weaken by at least one percent in 1997, improving competitiveness for exports but creating new presssure to raise wages.

---EU commissioners have dropped 53 out of the 58 cases of Danish shipbuilding subsidies they were investigating and have yet to reach a decision on the remaining five, which all involve Lindoe Vaerftet but have a combined value of onely one million crowns ($165,000)
